meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 先に到着して、今はホテルで休んでますよ。
examples.trans: She arrived ahead of you and is resting at the hotel right now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: 空いてるベッド用意させたの。看護婦にすごんだら一発。
examples.trans: I made them prepare an empty bed—one glare at the nurse did the trick.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 空いてるベッド用意させたの。看護婦にすごんだら一発。
examples.trans: I made them prepare an empty bed—one glare at the nurse did the trick.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).

examples.text: いっぱい作るのはいいんだけど、強い一発を見てえんだよ。
examples.trans: Making tons of tapes is fine, yet I want to see one powerhouse hit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 相変わらず落ち着きのない集団だね。
examples.trans: Still the same restless bunch as ever, huh.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 頼りにしてるよ。これからの売り上げはあいつらにかかってるからな。
examples.trans: I'm counting on him. Our future sales depend on those guys.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: sentence-final particle of emotion or reflection
meanings.note: Colloquial particle expressing sighing, wishing, or emphasis.

examples.text: いいなあ、うらやましい。

meanings.en: justification (申し訳ございません = no excuse / deeply sorry)
meanings.note: Paired with ございません or ありません for formal apologies.

examples.text: 遅れて申し訳ございません。
examples.trans: I am deeply sorry for being late.

examples.text: 大変申し訳ありませんでした。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: 相変わらず頼りになるなあ。本当に申し訳ない限りだ。
examples.trans: You are as reliable as ever. I truly cannot apologize enough.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

examples.text: 監督の村西だ。今回の作品は悪の組織と戦う超大作だ。
examples.trans: I'm Director Muranishi. This film is a blockbuster about fighting an evil organization.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Past 覚えた means 'I have memorized it' (and therefore now know it).

examples.text: 新しい言葉を覚えます。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: 覚えてるかな？村西さんがハワイで捕まった時のこと。
examples.trans: Do you remember when Mr. Muranishi was arrested overseas?

examples.text: いやそういう問題じゃねえ、捕まるぞおい！分かったよ！
examples.trans: That's not the issue—we're going to get arrested! Ugh, fine, I got the camera!

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。
全員が幸せになれる提案だよ、これは。
examples.trans: This is a proposal that makes everyone happy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Auxiliary godan verb following て-form.

examples.text: つい忘れてしまいました。
本を全部読んでしまった。
examples.trans: I finished reading the whole book.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 新しい商品を開発しています。
examples.trans: We are developing a new product.

examples.text: この商品はとても人気があります。

meanings.note: Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？
もちろん望むところです。
examples.trans: Of course—I wouldn't have it any other way.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Na-adjective.

examples.text: 特別な理由はありません。
日常と愛をつなぐ存在なんでございます。
examples.trans: I am here to bridge everyday life and human desire.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
